messages.subject: Examining sentences (not words) in R
messages.body_plain:
Greetings.

A colleague and I are looking at a corpus of learner writing and we want to determine the variability of sentence length under certain circumstances. So, how can I get R to consider the sentence as the basic unit of operation? I think this would entail using SCAN but with the SEP  argument to include periods, question marks and exclamation marks. I've played around trying to do this, but just get syntax errors.

A second problem is the ellipses, which, in ASCII at least, is three separate periods; plus there are many instances of '!!!!!' (at various lengths of course) and '...........................' and '?!?!?!??!' etc. Any ideas how I can handle these? (Preferably without going through the corpus and marking them up by hand, which I fear I may have to.)

--
Kevin Parent, Ph.D
VP-PR, Schoolmasters www.schoolmasters.ning.com <http://www.schoolmasters.ning.com>
National Korea Toastmasters webmaster www.koreatoastmasters.ning.com <http://www.koreatoastmasters.ning.com>

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Examining sentences (not words) in R
messages.subject_clean: [CorpLing with R] Examining sentences (not words) in R
messages.body_plain:
How about

- in a first step, loading the file and pasting it all together:
corpus <- paste(scan("something.txt", what=character(0), sep="\n"),
collapse=" ")

- in a second step, replacing ellipses etc. by 'tags' like this
corpus <- gsub("\\.{3}", "_ELLIPSIS_", corpus, perl=T)
# similar replacements for other things

- in a third step, using this to get 'sentences':
sentences <- unlist(strsplit(corpus, "[\\.\\;\\:\\?\\!]", perl=T))

STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
-----------------------------------------------
University of California, Santa Barbara
http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries
-----------------------------------------------

messages.body_plain:
Thanks! I had to tweak that a little (ellipses were sometimes four periods, sometimes five, etc.) but it works now.

Here's another question, maybe a little more challenging. In another project I'm working on, I want to find instances in which the same word is repeated immediately, such as 'boom boom' 'relax relax,' etc. Sometimes these are false starts, sometimes reduplication, sometimes for effect, so I think we'd have to ignore tags and punctuation as I wouldn't expect these to be tagged or punctuated consistently.

Any ideas how to do this?
